description: Create a meme on exactly one of: template (a catalog id), image (your own picture in base64 or a data: URL; JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF, up to 5 MB and 25 megapixels (16 for WebP, 8 for GIF, less for a large progressive JPEG), 100 px or more a side, at most 4:1; a GIF gives its first frame) or image_url (an https address the server downloads). Your own picture is laid out like a template, with slots found in it (see get_template). Captions go in slots, classic top/bottom positions or boxes (fractions of the image, x and y the top-left corner), plus optional author, emojis, stickers, shapes with text and a filter. The server fits and colours every caption, and may write a line break (\n) into a returned caption text, to keep a short word or a number off the end of a line, to keep a quote on one line or to break a long word after an underscore: a returned text sent back as it is comes out the same. With author, the handle goes in the first corner free of other layers, and of faces when it can: bottom right, top right, bottom left, top left. When a top and a bottom caption leave no corner free, the bottom one moves up a little to free one for the handle, given or saved by the person in the studio. Returns deliver (what to give the person), edit_url (opens the meme in the editor, never an image source), what each caption got, warnings and a picture: "preview" to check (800 px, or three frames of the clip if animated; the default with a template) or "final", the finished meme with the invisible watermark (1200 px, or an animated GIF if animated; the default with your own picture, as edit_url only reopens the captions). To send or save a file, with a terminal, do not paste base64 yourself: pipe the tools/call JSON from the shell into curl --data-binary @-, without a temporary copy of the picture, to the server's /mcp (Content-Type: application/json, Accept: application/json, text/event-stream; no initialize needed), then decode the data of the image item in result.content from base64 into a file for the person.

author.description: The person's handle, with or without @, only if they gave it

height.description: Box height, fraction of the height

max_size.description: Largest text size, 1 = the usual meme size

position.description: Classic placement on a single photo; ignored with slot or x and y

slot.description: Slot number or name from get_template

style.description: outline, plain or box (text on a solid box)

text.description: The caption, under the fits_chars of its slot. \n forces a line break. It is written in capitals

width.description: Box width, fraction of the width (0.9 by default)

x.description: Left edge of the box, fraction of the width

y.description: Top edge of the box, fraction of the height

center_y.description: From the top: 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom; a larger value moves it down

emoji.description: One of the emojis Meme Studio offers

filter_strength.description: 0 to 1; the studio default when missing

image.description: Your own picture instead of a template: JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF in base64 (a data: URL works too), up to 5 MB and 25 megapixels (16 for WebP, 8 for GIF, less for a large progressive JPEG)

image_url.description: Your own picture instead of a template: an https address the server downloads

language.description: Language of the person: es opens the Spanish studio, en the English one

picture.description: preview: to check, 800 px or three frames of an animated template (the default with a template); final: the finished meme, 1200 px or an animated GIF (the default with image or image_url)

flip.description: Mirror it; the bubble tail goes to the right

center_y.description: From the top: 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom; a larger value moves it down

template.description: Template id; or give image or image_url instead

name: create_meme
